Below, my system characteristics

Operating System: Fedora Linux 40
KDE Plasma Version: 6.0.4
KDE Frameworks Version: 6.1.0
Qt Version: 6.7.0
Kernel Version: 6.8.8-300.fc40.x86_64 (64-bit)
Graphics Platform: X11

Could you please assist me?
Cheers,
Alejandro

messages.body_plain:
Regarding the issue of Kate addons not working/integrating into RKWard.

I have noticed the same thing.  For me seems to be recent - probably 
related to the KDE6 upgrade.  I delayed upgrading to the latest KDE6 for 
as long as possible as I knew it would break things.  However, other 
essential software I use forced an upgrade to fix a problem.

Looking at: 
https://mail.kde.org/pipermail/rkward-tracker/2024-April/010660.html

Seems Kate plugin path may have changed?

I can still use RKWard as I normally do - so apart from the annoyance - 
it doesn't seem to be a show-stopper?

We might just have to wait for an updated version of RKWard.

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

On Wed, 08 May 2024 01:08:03 +0100
"rkward @ oijn" <rkward-users at oijn.uk> wrote:
> Seems Kate plugin path may have changed?

yes, but more importantly kate is now based on KF6/Qt6, and so the
kate plugins will not work with a KF5/Qt5 version of RKWard. I'm working
on a KF6 version, but it will be some more time before a release.

If you are willing to compile from source, you can use a KF6 RKWard,
today, and this should indeed be pretty stable, already (on Linux).

For this you'll need the master git branch from
https://invent.kde.org/education/rkward

Generic instructions for building from source can be found at
https://rkward.kde.org/Building_RKWard_From_Source.html
although the package names and versions to install will no longer be
correct. Don't hesitate to ask for assistance with that!

Regards
Thomas

messages.body_plain:
On Thu, 9 May 2024 11:09:22 +0200
Thomas Friedrichsmeier <thomas.friedrichsmeier at kdemail.net> wrote:
> If you are willing to compile from source, you can use a KF6 RKWard,
> today, and this should indeed be pretty stable, already (on Linux).

I will add, there are now (development snapshot) AppImages of RKWard KF6
that are expected to work on a wide range of distributions:

https://cdn.kde.org/ci-builds/education/rkward/master/linux/

After downloading, you'll have to chmod u+x the downloaded file.

IMPORTANT: While the AppImage embeds an installation of R, this is
quite limited in functionality, for technical reasons. Importantly, you
will not be able to install most R packages. However, you can run the
AppImage as:

./rkward-xyz-AppImage --r-executable /usr/bin/R

to use your system installed full-featured R. (This is still
fairly fresh, and admittedly still somewhat experimental, therefore no
UI support for selecting the R version, so far).

Regards
Thomas
